Definition: What proportion of the population does the register cover?
Comments: Vital Statistics Report 2018-2021 provides registration completeness from NPRS; births completeness 62.0% (2021) and deaths 97.6% (2021). Using birth completeness as proxy gives 50-69% category.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Changed from 4 to 3. NSA's own Vital Statistics Report shows birth-registration completeness fell to 62.0% in 2021 (from 89.6% in 2020), and NSA officials reported in mid-2026 that birth-certificate coverage for children aged 0-8 had further declined to 53-54% by 2023. Both figures sit in the 50-69% band, not 70-89%; the original comment itself flagged the 62% figure but the code was never corrected.

Evidence is mixed: ECN requires a national ID/passport as proof of identity for registration, but the World Bank's ID4D identity-system analysis states ECN's digital fingerprint capture and MHAI's AFIS are separate systems with no data layer for exporting/sharing fingerprints — i.e. no confirmed technical/database linkage to the national ID system, only a documentary requirement. redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Changed from 2 (Planned) to 4 (Partially deployed). The Integrated Social Assistance System (ISAS), linked to the NPRS, was developed, launched and piloted in 2022 (HPPII activity tracker, marked 'Complete') and is now in active use — a March 2026 Cabinet decision on the Conditional Basic Income Grant confirms ISAS is implemented and used to verify identity/life-status and pay beneficiaries.
